original_question: Use the Perron Frobenius spectral theory of positive C0 -groups to characterize unitary C0 -groups on a Hilbert space H that are unitarily isomorphic to a Koopman group on an L2 -space.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 18 ("Characterizing Koopman groups on Hilbert spaces").
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially the paper’s Problem 18 almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the intended method (the Perron-Frobenius spectral theory of positive C0-groups), the class to be characterized (unitary C0-groups on a Hilbert space H), and the target model class (those unitarily isomorphic to a Koopman group on an L2-space).
missing_details: The one-parameter group structure is implicit: a C0-group means a strongly continuous family (U_t)_{t in R} of bounded operators with U_{t+s}=U_t U_s and U_0=I.

The paper does not spell out the meaning of 'Koopman group'; to make the question stand-alone, this should be stated as a group induced by a measurable measure-preserving flow (phi_t)_{t in R} on some measure space (X, Sigma, mu), acting by composition on L2(X, Sigma, mu).
The phrase 'unitarily isomorphic' should be made explicit as the existence of a unitary intertwining operator W:H->L2(X,Sigma,mu) such that W U_t W^{-1} equals the Koopman operator for every t in R.
The ambient L2-space is unspecified in the paper; a self-contained version should say 'for some measure space (X, Sigma, mu)' without adding extra restrictions not present in the paper.

The order structure behind 'positive C0-groups' is implicit; positivity is with respect to the usual positive cone on an L2-space (or, more generally, on a Banach lattice), but the paper does not specify a narrower framework here.
The problem says 'characterize' but does not explicitly say 'necessary and sufficient conditions'; making that explicit improves stand-alone clarity while staying faithful to the paper.
The scalar field of H is not stated in Problem 18; in semigroup/operator-theoretic usage it is usually complex, but this remains implicit in the paper.
refined_question: Use the Perron-Frobenius spectral theory of positive C0-groups to give necessary and sufficient conditions for a unitary C0-group (U_t)_{t in R} on a Hilbert space H to be unitarily isomorphic to a Koopman C0-group on some L2-space; equivalently, characterize exactly when there exist a measure space (X, Sigma, mu), a measurable measure-preserving flow (phi_t)_{t in R}, and a unitary operator W:H->L2(X,Sigma,mu) such that, for every t in R, W U_t W^{-1} is the Koopman operator f |-> f o phi_t on L2(X,Sigma,mu).
justification: The arXiv paper is a collection of open problems, not a theorem paper, and your draft clearly targets Section 4 rather than any introduction-level conjecture/theorem framework. The exact match is Problem 18 in Section 4, whose wording is already very close to your draft. There is no nearby proposition, theorem, or remark in the paper giving a sharper equivalent reformulation of this particular item, so the appropriate refinement is to keep the scope exactly the same and only make the hidden definitions explicit: what a C0-group is, what a Koopman group on an L2-space means, and what 'unitarily isomorphic' means. I therefore did not broaden the problem beyond the paper’s stated aim and did not add assumptions on separability, sigma-finiteness, probability normalization, or a fixed underlying measure space, since the paper itself does not impose them.
